key: Of whom, the Terrible, they ask, Where is He? or verily they say of him, He is not. He sweeps away, like birds, the foe’s possessions. Have faith in him, for He, O men, is Indra.
s: In a hymn whose refrain names Indra to the people, this verse meets those who doubt him; Sāyaṇa, on 2.12.5, reads the doubters as those who, not seeing him, think him nowhere, and the verse as bidding trust that Indra is, though not plainly seen.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.12.5, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401594 (2024)

evidence.words: अपश्यंतो जना घोरं शत्रूणां घातकं यं पृच्छंति स्म कुह सेति । स इंद्रः कुत्र वर्तत इति … न क्वचिदसौ तिष्ठतीति मन्यमाना जना एनमिंद्रमाहुः एष इंद्रो नास्तीति … तस्माद् श्रदस्मा इंद्राय धत्त। स इंद्रोऽस्तीति विश्वासमत्र कुरुत । यद्यप्यसौ विशेषतोऽस्माभिर्न दृश्यते तथापि अस्तीति विश्वासं कुरुत
evidence.gloss: People who do not see him ask of the terrible one, the slayer of foes, Where is he, that is, where does Indra dwell ... Thinking he stays nowhere, people say of this Indra, this Indra is not ... Therefore put faith in this Indra: have trust here that Indra is. Even though he is not distinctly seen by us, still have trust that he is.

reason: The problem holds: ‘names Indra to the people’ and ‘reads the doubters as people who’ doubled the word and made the doubters seem the refrain’s addressees. Changed ‘people who’ to ‘those who’; 45 words. Re-opened packet.js veda 27 --verse 2.12.5: Sāyaṇa has the askers as those who do not see him (अपश्यंतो जना), saying Indra is not because they think he stays nowhere (न क्वचिदसौ तिष्ठतीति मन्यमाना), and bids trust that he is though not distinctly seen (यद्यप्यसौ विशेषतोऽस्माभिर्न दृश्यते तथापि अस्तीति विश्वासं कुरुत); evidence verbatim, reading unchanged. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 2.12.5, at [202,5]); entry-check ok.
